prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, three-quarter-length demi statue portrait — a sculpted figure ending at the knee. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips right at the knee, where the leg would bend, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her knees, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Norwegian woman in Nordic valkyrie makeup — fair skin with a light scatter of freckles, strong straight defined dark-blonde brows, warm bronze shadow across the lids, a fine brown liner, long lashes, large pale-blue eyes with bright real catchlights, soft contour, a muted red-brown lip, long pale-blonde hair in two thick braids and a braided crown, a fierce, steady, commanding expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a thick silver knotted hoop.

Physique: A colossal rounded chest, an enormous belly of massive rounded folds hanging low and heavy, no waist at all, colossal wide hips flaring beyond the chest and massive thick thighs disappearing out of the bottom of the frame.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — both shoulders, both arms and hands, her chest, belly, hips and both distinct thighs down to the knee — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically carved from ONE solid block of genuine labradorite, a deep grey stone that flashes brilliant streaks of blue and green light across its surface as it catches the light, polished to a hard glossy sheen, completely opaque. It is one continuous sculpted mass, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same stone, the flashing colour running unbroken across every joint. Right at the knee, where the leg would naturally bend, each thigh individually curves inward and rounds off into its own smooth, polished tip, the flashing colour converging at its centre — the two thighs stay clearly separate all the way down, never merging, fusing or tapering into a single base — no calves, no feet, nothing continues below either tip — the stone simply reaching its natural end on each leg, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Opacity: everything below the collarbones is solid, completely opaque labradorite — no light passes through it at any point. It has the same cool, hard, dense solidity throughout, catching light only as bright highlights on its polished surface, never glowing from within. Her face, by contrast, is warm, soft, living flesh, its natural colour nowhere close to the colour of the stone.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the stone's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded tip at the end of each thigh is the material's own carved finish, always the clean, deliberate result of a sculpture — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a cold slate grey on one side and a shifting blue-green flash on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (solid material) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand (solid material) relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so slate-grey light glances off the left half and blue-green light glances off the right half, catching in bright reflections. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. Only her face, ears and neck read as real skin. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
